title: Day 38 · Week 5, Day 3 — Parents: sex, sleep and stress in the first trimester — what the cohorts actually find, and the one variable that moves the outcomes
summary: The second Parents episode. Your baby is 2.5–4.5 mm at Carnegie stage 11, the rostral neuropore closing and the heart looped and beating. Sex: half of women worry it will harm the pregnancy and only 29% ever discuss it with a clinician (Bartellas 2000); the NHS position is that it is safe unless told otherwise, with the exceptions specific and mostly later; 59 studies find no harm without risk factors (von Sydow 1999); in a UK case-control study of 6,719 women, feeling well enough for sex went with less miscarriage, not more (Maconochie 2007), and the same reverse-causation pattern holds for preterm birth (Sayle 2001). Bleeding: 27% of 4,510 women bled in the first trimester; spotting carried no measurable excess risk (OR 1.1), heavy bleeding with pain tripled it (Hasan 2009) — so every episode gets a call and almost none is bad news. Desire goes up in some women and down in most; what couples lack is the conversation. Sleep: 76% poor quality, 38% insufficient, 100% waking, 78% napping, in every month of pregnancy (Mindell 2015, 2,427 women) — the split starts now. The relationship: the measured decline is after the birth and pre-pregnancy satisfaction and planning protect against it (Lawrence 2008, 156 couples); emotional intimacy and conflict management move satisfaction more than sex does (Ramsdell 2020, 154 couples); first-time fathers already cut their drinking most (MoBa, 82,362 couples). Stress, read honestly: miscarriage OR 1.42 in a meta-analysis of eight mostly retrospective studies; the bereavement registers (3 million and 4.9 million births) as the ceiling — stillbirth +18%, preterm +7%; anxiety symptoms with no association to perinatal outcomes across 50 studies; child cognition r = −0.05. The buffer in every study is the relationship.
action: Tonight, one conversation, fifteen minutes, three questions you ask: (1) about sex this trimester — what do you want, and what should I stop guessing about? — and take the answer as the week's rule; (2) what time do you want to be asleep by this week? — set it as the household bedtime and end the evening there; (3) what is the one thing on your list I could just take? — take it by the weekend. If there has been any bleeding, the fourth question is for the practice in the morning, not for her.
